pc.pc: Whether you are taking this training because you need to or you just want to learn more, rest assured you have made the right choice.
The concepts you will learn today will help you make better decisions about responsible alcohol service.

Believe it or not, simple everyday decisions could have far-reaching implications not only for your restaurant and your community, but also for you. When you serve alcohol, you are personally liable for any adverse consequences resulting from your decisions.

pc.pc: Alcohol consumption is a common practice in the U.S. People often enjoy a beverage while attending social functions, gathering with friends at a bar or restaurant, or simply to accompany a meal. As a result, alcohol sales are one way for businesses to attract patrons, boost sales, and increase profit.

pc.pc: Economic Impact of the Alcohol Industry

originalData.data: <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20" SpacingBefore="6" SpacingAfter="0"><ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" Color="#000000" BulletFont="Arial" /></Style>

pc.pc: According to the Economic Impact Study conducted by America’s Beer, Wine & Spirits Retailers in 2018, the retail alcohol industry generates over 2.03 million jobs in the U.S. and has an estimated direct economic impact of $122.63 billion per year. This includes both on-premise and off-premise alcohol sales.

pc.pc: Excessive consumption can lead to serious negative consequences.

originalData.data: <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Single" LineSpacing="20" SpacingBefore="6" SpacingAfter="0"><ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /></Style>

pc.pc: In moderation, alcoholic beverages can be a source of pleasure, helping some people relax or feel more sociable. However, excessive consumption can lead to serious negative consequences, not only for the person who consumes the alcohol, but to others surrounding them.

He was sentenced to 20 years in prison for the crime of vehicular homicide.
He had consumed 12 cocktails earlier that day and was driving with a BAC of over twice the legal limit. He was also driving at a speed of over 100 mph on a 40 mph road.

pc.pc: Nearly 95,000 people die prematurely in the U.S. from alcohol related causes each year. (CDC), making alcohol the third-leading cause of preventable deaths. In California, an average of 15,443 people died from alcohol related causes between 2015 and 2019, 384 of which were under 21 years old.

pc.pc: In 2010, alcohol misuse cost the United States $249 billion in health care expenses, law enforcement and justice expenses, losses in workplace productivity, and losses from motor vehicle accidents.
Most people who binge drink don’t have an alcohol use disorder. And yet, 77% of these costs are a result of binge drinking.
Source: https://www.cdc.gov/alcohol/features/excessive-drinking.html

pc.pc: Those are some pretty alarming statistics, but the good news is that you can take an active role in protecting your customers and those around them.
Your job is not only to make sure that patrons have a good time, but to also prevent them from causing any harm to themselves or others.
If you neglect this aspect of your job, the consequences could be devastating.

pc.pc: According to the Centers for Disease Control, binge drinking increases the risk of violent or reckless behavior leading to both intentional and unintentional injuries, such as car accidents, homicides, suicides, domestic violence, child abuse, child neglect, and assault, including sexual assault.
As you can imagine, these incidents also have a direct impact on calls to first responders, such as law enforcement, fire departments, and emergency medical transporters.
In fact, in 2020, alcohol was responsible for 5% of the visits to the emergency room reported in the State of California.

Source: Health Care Almanac, California Health and Human Services Agency. (n.d.). Alcohol-Related Emergency Department Encounters in California, 2020. Retrieved from https://hcai.ca.gov/visualizations/alcohol-related-emergency-department-encounters-in-california-2020/#:~:text=to%20Featured%20Releases-,Alcohol%2DRelated%20Emergency%20Department%20Encounters%20in%20California%2C%202020,nearly%2012%20million%20total%20encounters.

Driving above the legal limit is a serious offense punishable by suspension of a driver’s license, expensive fines, and in more serious cases, possible jail time.

pc.pc: Establishments are also responsible for maintaining a safe, non-disruptive environment for both patrons and surrounding neighbors. This is because alcohol abuse also impacts the quality of life in the neighborhood, leading to higher crime rates, public indecency, littering, noise, property damage, and other disturbances
Establishments must take all necessary measures to prevent unruly behavior inside the establishment, such as fights, assaults, prostitution, or alcohol intoxication.
Customers making loud noise, playing loud music, loitering, littering, or engaging in vandalism outside of the establishment are also considered disturbances.

As a server, it is important that you keep an eye out for these types of behaviors to avoid potential fines. It is the Alcohol Server's responsibility to the community as the gatekeepers of persons obtaining alcohol in public.

pc.pc: From a public health standpoint, both alcohol use disorder (alcoholism) and binge drinking are associated with a long list of health conditions and risk factors.

Short term effects include alcohol poisoning, fetal alcohol spectrum disorders, stillbirths, miscarriages, sexually transmitted diseases caused by risky sexual behavior, violent and even suicidal behaviors in some individuals.

pc.pc: What are the effects of alcohol? And why does it produce possible intoxication?
Let’s take a look. Ethyl alcohol, also known as ethanol, is the active intoxicating ingredient found in all alcoholic beverages, such as beer, wine, and liquor.
Alcohol is the result of the fermentation process of yeast, sugar, or starch. Wine and cider are made by fermenting fruit. Beer and liquor are produced by fermenting grains, such as barley or rye.

pc.pc: Finally, once in the bloodstream, alcohol quickly reaches the brain and produces symptoms such as slurred speech, poor coordination, relaxed inhibitions, and a general sense of well-being.
Alcohol depresses the central nervous system’s functions. This
impairs judgement, slows down reaction times, and reduces vision, coordination, and concentration. That’s why driving while intoxicated is so dangerous.

pc.pc: You may have also heard about other ‘techniques’ to reduce intoxication, such as:
Taking a cold shower
Doing physical activity
Taking deep breaths
Urinating
Drinking an energy drink while drinking alcohol
These are all common beliefs. Unfortunately, once alcohol has entered the body, all you can do to reduce levels of intoxication is to wait it out. Why?

pc.pc: Because most of the alcohol (about 90%) is metabolized by the liver, and the liver is only capable of breaking down alcohol at the rate of one drink per hour. The liver does not speed up when there is excessive alcohol in the bloodstream.

The liver is responsible for maintaining blood sugar levels, but when alcohol is present, the liver puts normal functions on hold to metabolize alcohol from the bloodstream. Alcohol also depletes the body of fluids causing thirst and dehydration.

We will cover what is considered a drink later in the training. But now that you know this, you probably understand why it is important that you serve drinks to customers at a rate that makes it possible for their livers to metabolize the alcohol.

Drinking too much in a short period of time will make it impossible for their liver to keep up, and will inevitably result in intoxication. Intoxication can occur in as little as one alcoholic drink equivalent or standard drink.

pc.pc: Definition of Alcohol Intoxication for the Purpose of DUI

originalData.data: <Style LineSpacingRule="Single" />
<Style FontFamily="Articulate Light" FontSize="12" ForegroundColor="dk1,00" LinkColor="dk1,00" />
<Style LineSpacingRule="Single" />

<Style FontFamily="Articulate Light" FontSize="12" FontIsBold="False" FontIsItalic="False" FontIsUnderline="False" FontIsStrikeout="False" ForegroundColor="dk1,00" LinkColor="dk1,00" />

pc.pc: The definition of alcohol intoxication for the purpose of determining if someone is driving under the influence (DUI) is: “a state where mental and/or physical faculties are impaired to such a degree that you no longer have the ability to drive with the caution characteristic of a sober person.”
In the state of California (and in all 50 states) it is illegal to operate a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration, BAC, of 0.08% or higher.

pc.pc: BAC is used to measure the difference between the rate at which alcohol is absorbed and the rate at which it is eliminated.
This standard is used to measure and predict the level of impairment that can be expected after consuming alcohol.

pc.pc: It is very important that you remember one thing, though.
The rate of absorption is not the same for all individuals. It varies from person to person depending on several factors.
Let's learn more about this.

pc.pc: The second factor is drinking rate. A person who consumes alcohol in a short period of time will always have a higher BAC than a person who consumes the same amount over a longer period of time.
This is simply because your body needs time to metabolize alcohol.
If you drink at a higher rate than your liver can process, which is approximately one drink per hour, your BAC will continue to rise.
Binge drinking can quickly lead to higher levels of intoxication.

pc.pc: Food intake is another variable to remember. Drinking on an empty stomach will cause a faster increase in your BAC.
People who have eaten food, especially foods high in protein and/or fat, will normally have a lower BAC.
The reason for this is that the presence of food in the stomach slows down alcohol absorption. Why?
Because the pyloric valve at the bottom of the stomach closes in order to keep food there for digestion, and in doing this, it also keeps alcohol from reaching the small intestine.

pc.pc: Gender also plays a significant role. In general, women tend to have a higher BAC than men.
This is because men usually have a lower body fat percentage and larger body mass, which allows their bodies to metabolize alcohol faster than women’s.
In addition to this, women usually produce less of an enzyme called dehydrogenase, which is responsible for breaking down alcohol in the stomach.

pc.pc: The next factor is body composition, which refers to the amount of fat versus the amount of lean muscle in a person’s body.
An individual with a higher body fat percentage will have a higher BAC than a person of the same size who has a lower body fat percentage. Why?
Because body fat does not absorb alcohol, which results in alcohol circulating in the bloodstream for a longer period of time.

pc.pc: You must also consider the person’s age.
As people age, the amount of water in the body and lean body mass decreases, which results in an increase in body fat.
Since a higher body fat percentage slows down alcohol absorption, seniors will tend to have a higher BAC than their younger counterparts.

pc.pc: Fatigue and Illness also have an impact on a person's BAC. When you are sick, you are likely to become dehydrated, which means there is less water available in your body for the alcohol to become diluted.
In addition to this, both fatigue and dehydration can cause the liver to become less efficient at eliminating alcohol.
Other illnesses, such as genetic enzyme deficiencies, diabetes, or hypertension may also interfere with the body’s ability to metabolize alcohol.

Another factor to take into account is that alcohol acts as a depressant of the limbic system, the area of the brain responsible for regulating emotions, often causing our emotions to become intensified.

pc.pc: Finally, it is important to mention that some medications can have adverse effects and often dangerous interactions with alcohol.
This includes over-the-counter medications, such as acetaminophen, or common antihistamines, such as cold or allergy pills.
When mixed with alcohol, acetaminophen can lead to severe liver damage.
Antihistamines, on the other hand, can have a sedative effect which would heighten the depressant effects of alcohol.

It is extremely dangerous to combine alcohol with any sort of substance, prescription or non-prescription. This includes any medication, recreational and illegal drugs, which could lead to unpleasant side effects and even death when mixed with alcohol.

pc.pc: The woman on the right had twice as much to drink as the woman on the left.

The woman on the left ordered steak, while the woman on the right ordered a salad. Compared to a salad, a steak is much higher in protein and fat. Foods high in protein and fat take longer to digest, therefore slowing down alcohol absorption.

pc.pc: Common telltale signs include recklessness with money, such as someone offering to buy drinks for strangers, impaired judgement, inability to assess risks, lack of eye contact, and relaxed inhibitions, such as acting overly friendly, affectionate, or animated.

Individuals may also appear forgetful, drowsy, anxious or depressed. In some cases, they may display signs of aggression, make irrational statements, become rude or argumentative, or complain about the strength of the drink being served.
Finally, you should pay attention to any sudden changes in attitude or mood

pc.pc: For example, if a patron who initially comes across as shy and rather reserved later starts getting overly friendly with you or other guests, you have good reason to suspect that the person is intoxicated.
Use of foul language, increased volume when speaking, and an increased rate of alcohol consumption are signs of lowered inhibitions.
And remember, a drastic change in a person’s behavior is more important to be aware of than the behavior itself.

pc.pc: People often refer to tolerance as the ability to ‘handle their alcohol’.
However, there is an important distinction to be made.
Alcohol tolerance, often called functional tolerance, does not equal a low BAC.

Tolerance refers to the body’s acclimation to alcohol consumption or other toxic substances. It varies from one person to another and it can build up over time. Increased tolerance lessens the effects of alcohol on the central nervous system.
The more a person drinks, the less they feel the effects of alcohol, and the better they get at concealing signs of impairment.
However, this does not mean that their BAC is within the legal limit.
Chronic heavy drinkers may look calm and collected, but their BAC may be just as high, or even higher, than that of the loud customer you had to cut off the other night.

pc.pc: In addition to this, research shows that functional tolerance is not developed at the same rate for all alcohol effects.
That is to say that, while a person may be competent enough to perform intellectual tasks, they may be impaired to complete others that require coordination and motor skills, such as driving.

pc.pc: In summary, you should always stop service to intoxicated customers. It doesn’t matter if they are regulars, accompanied by someone, or not planning to drive themselves home.
As we have learned, alcohol intoxication can lead to dangerous consequences and it is your job to prevent it no matter the circumstances.

pc.pc: A medical bracelet does not mean you can discriminate and refuse alcohol service.
However, being aware can improve your ability to take action in the event of a medical emergency.

pc.pc: Before we move on to the next section, it is worth mentioning that disability or illness can occasionally be confused with intoxication.

Before you make assumptions, conduct an initial assessment and notice any medical jewelry, such as a diabetic bracelet. Remember, a medical bracelet does not mean you can discriminate and refuse alcohol service.
However, being aware of this can improve your ability to take action in the event of a medical emergency. It might save someone’s life.
Now, let’s move to some review questions.

pc.pc: In this section, we will spend some time reviewing the different laws and regulations that pertain to alcohol service in the State of California.

Let’s start with some definitions contained in Title 4 of the California Code of Regulations, which are used by the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control to interpret and enforce the Business and Professions Code.
Click on each button to review the definition. When you are done, click on the button on the bottom right to continue.

pc.pc: (b) (1) A licensee that is subject to this article shall ensure that each alcohol server it employs has a valid alcohol server certification.
The licensee shall maintain records of certifications for inspection, upon request, by the department.

(2) Except for a violation of subdivision (c), it shall be a defense against any action for a violation of this article that the alcohol server was within 60 calendar days of initial employment or, with regard to employees employed prior to July 1, 2022, between July 1, 2022, and August 31, 2022, inclusive.

pc.pc: a) Beginning July 1, 2022, a licensee that is subject to this article shall not employ or continue to employ any alcohol server without a valid alcohol server certification.
(1) An alcohol server who was employed by the licensee prior to July 1, 2022, shall obtain an alcohol server certification by August 31, 2022.
(2) An alcohol server who is employed by the licensee on or after July 1, 2022, shall obtain an alcohol server certification within
60 calendar
days of employment.

pc.pc: Why is this new requirement so important? Let’s take a look at a hypothetical scenario.
A 20-year old woman visits a college bar with a group of friends. They order a few rounds of cocktails and are having a good time.
The server in charge of the table later remembers that the 20-year old girl also ordered 2 shots of vodka and started dancing on one of the tables.
The club staff asks her to come down and she is visibly upset, but her friends eventually convince her to do so. She leaves the bar shortly after and drives home.

pc.pc: When we talk about liability, we refer to the legal responsibility of an individual as it relates to alcohol service.
There are three areas of liability: administrative, civil, and criminal.
Liability is when you are held responsible for any injuries suffered by your patrons, or damages or injuries caused by them.
Let's talk about administrative liability.

pc.pc: Administrative Liability is the most common form of liability for businesses serving alcohol. It extends to the licensee who holds a permit to sell and/or serve alcohol.

Alcohol-related laws are enforced by state and local law enforcement agencies who regulate the production, sale, and distribution of alcohol within its borders. The regulatory authority in California is the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control or ABC.
When a liquor license is issued, the permit holder is expected to abide by certain regulations such as:
checking IDs
refusing service to underage or intoxicated guests.
operating only within permitted hours

pc.pc: Failure to comply with such regulations can result in administrative penalties for an establishment. Penalties are determined by the CA ABC on a case-by-case basis, taking into account the nature of the violation, and any history of previous violations.
Some examples of administrative penalties include fines between $750 to $6,000, suspension, and even revocation of the liquor license.
The purpose of these penalties is not to punish, but to prevent licensees from using license privileges in ways that are illegal and harmful to the community.

pc.pc: Criminal liability results from breaking state, county, or municipal law by selling alcohol irresponsibly.
In this case, the State will most likely bring a lawsuit against the individual who furnished the alcohol for what is considered an act against society.
Depending on the seriousness of the offense, the server and owner can face fines, community service, and even possible jail time.
For example, if a minor consumes alcohol and is then injured or killed or injures a third party, the person who furnished the alcohol will face 6 to 12 months in jail and fines of up to $1,000

pc.pc: Felonies are the most serious crimes and are punishable by imprisonment.
California defines felonies as crimes that carry a maximum sentence of more than 1 year. They include the sale of illegal drugs, murder, rape, robbery.
Penalties include imprisonment at a
state prison or county jail and fines up to $10,000.
The most serious offenses could be punished by a life sentence or the death penalty.

pc.pc: Misdemeanors are mid-level criminal offenses, more serious than infractions, but less serious than felonies.

Misdemeanors include public drunkenness, drug possession, driving under the influence, disorderly conduct, furnishing alcohol to a minor or an obviously intoxicated person, employing minors at establishments who are primarily engaged in the sale and service of alcohol, serving alcohol outside of permitted hours, shoplifting, and petty theft.
Misdemeanors are punishable by fines of up to
$1,000 and 6 months
to one year in county jail, based on the seriousness of the offense. Depending on the case, probation, community service, or restitution to the victim may also be mandated by the courts.

pc.pc: Infractions are the least serious of offenses.
They include most traffic violations like driving above the speed limit, running a red light, or parking in a forbidden area.
They are not punishable by jail time and penalties include
fines not to exceed $250.

pc.pc: Civil cases, on the other hand, involve disputes between two private parties.

Based on this definition, civil liability means that an employee or the owner of an establishment can be held liable for any injury or damage caused to a third party by an intoxicated guest if their actions contributed to the injury, or if they failed to take action to prevent it.

pc.pc: You may have also heard the term ‘Dram shop law’.
The word ‘dram’ is an English term used to refer to a unit of volume when measuring alcohol.
In the U.S. ‘Dram shop’ refers to an establishment where a patron is served alcohol even after showing clear signs of intoxication.
‘Dram shop laws’ impose civil liability by holding businesses strictly liable to any third parties injured by a drunken patron. What does this mean?

It means that a business and the employees working there can be sued by a third party who may have suffered injuries as a result of the actions of an intoxicated guest, even if that third party never set foot in the establishment.
Simply put, the premise behind dram shop laws is that a business owner is responsible for the safety of both patrons and all other third parties encountered by them.
Dram shop laws vary from one state to another, with some states enforcing stricter standards.
However, dram shop laws in general seek to promote responsible alcohol service practices among establishments.

pc.pc: California removed the strict liability dram shop law from the civil code.
One Exception:
Any person who serves alcohol to a visibly intoxicated person
under the age of 21
is to be held strictly liable for any injuries caused by the drunk minor.

pc.pc: Although the State of California removed the strict liability dram shop law from the civil code, there is still one exception.

Per Section 25602.1 of the Business and Professions Code, any person who serves alcohol to a visibly intoxicated person under the age of 21 is to be held strictly liable for any injuries caused by the drunk minor.

pc.pc: Notwithstanding subdivision (b) of Section 25602,
a cause of action may be brought by or on behalf of any person who has suffered injury or death against any person licensed
, or required to be licensed, pursuant to Section 23300, or any person authorized by the federal government to sell alcoholic beverages on a military base or other federal enclave,
who sells
, furnishes, gives or causes to be sold, furnished or given away any alcoholic beverage,
and any other person who sells
, or causes to be sold,
any alcoholic beverage, to any obviously intoxicated minor
where the furnishing, sale or giving of that beverage to the minor is the proximate cause of the personal injury or death sustained by that person.

pc.pc: Exercise Reasonable Care

<Style FontFamily="Articulate Light" FontSize="12" FontIsBold="False" FontIsItalic="False" FontIsUnderline="False" ForegroundColor="dk1,00" LinkColor="dk1,00" />

pc.pc: But just because civil liability is limited to serving underage patrons, this doesn’t mean that you should throw caution to the wind. Under common law duties of care, licensees should exercise reasonable care to keep their customers safe. If the licensee is found negligent when serving alcohol, civil liability can result even if the person they serve is not a minor.

Reckless conduct is another reason that may lead to a lawsuit. Reckless conduct is more serious than negligence, as it implies that the person acted deliberately, disregarding a risk that they were or should have been aware of.
Penalties for civil liability are generally monetary payments to individuals who bring the civil lawsuit.

pc.pc: Any licensee who hires a person under 21 to prepare or serve alcohol at an establishment whose primary business is the sale and service of alcohol will be charged with a misdemeanor.
Persons between 18 and 21 years old may work and serve alcohol at establishments licensed to sell alcohol if:
The primary purpose of the business is to serve food, and
The person performs their duties in an area used primarily for food service.

pc.pc: In California, public intoxication is a misdemeanor.
To be considered
drunk in public
someone must be intoxicated in a public place
AND
be
unable to exercise care for their own safety or the safety of others, or interfere with the use of the street, sidewalk, or other public area.

pc.pc: Anyone who provides alcohol to a habitual drunkard or obviously intoxicated person is guilty of a misdemeanor.
A
habitual drunkard
is defined as someone who is not able to control his or her drinking. You may find out in two ways:
A family member tells you that the person has a drinking problem and asks you not to serve them.
The patron is a regular who frequently loses control over their drinking
Someone is
o
bviously intoxicated
when the average person can plainly see that they are drunk.

pc.pc: KEY TAKEAWAYS
The following are also guilty of a misdemeanor:
Anyone who allows a minor to enter and remain at an establishment whose primary business is to sell or serve alcohol without a legitimate business reason, such as making a delivery.
A minor who enters and remains in a licensed establishment without a legitimate business reason.

pc.pc: KEY TAKEAWAYS
All of the following will be guilty of a misdemeanor:
Anyone who sells or provides alcohol to minors under 21.
Anyone who provides alcohol to a minor who suffers an injury or injures someone else after consuming the alcohol.
Licensees who allow a minor to consume alcohol in their establishment, even if unaware that the person is a minor.

pc.pc: (a) Except as provided in subdivision (c), no licensee that sells or serves alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises shall employ any person under 21 years of age for the purpose of preparing or serving alcoholic beverages. Every person who employs or uses the services of any person under the age of 21 years in or on that portion of any premises, during business hours, which are primarily designed and used for the sale and service of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) Any person between 18 and 21 years of age employed in any bona fide public eating place, as defined in Sections 23038 and 23038.1, which is licensed for the on-sale of alcoholic beverages, may serve alcoholic beverages to consumers only under the following circumstances: such service occurs in an area primarily designed and used for the sale and service of food for consumption on the premises; and the primary duties of the employee shall be the service of meals to guests, with the service of alcoholic beverages being incidental to such duties. For purposes of this subdivision, “serve” or “service” includes the delivery, presentation, opening, or pouring of an alcoholic beverage.

pc.pc: Except as provided in subdivision (l), every person who commits any of the following acts is guilty of disorderly conduct, a misdemeanor.

(f) Who is found in any public place under the influence of intoxicating liquor, any drug, controlled substance, toluene, or any combination of any intoxicating liquor, drug, controlled substance, or toluene, in a condition that he or she is unable to exercise care for his or her own safety or the safety of others, or by reason of his or her being under the influence of intoxicating liquor, any drug, controlled substance, toluene, or any combination of any intoxicating liquor, drug, or toluene, interferes with or obstructs or prevents the free use of any street, sidewalk, or other public way.

pc.pc: Every person who sells, furnishes, gives, or causes to be sold, furnished, or given away, any alcoholic beverage to any habitual or common drunkard or to any obviously intoxicated person is guilty of a misdemeanor.

pc.pc: Any licensee under an on-sale license issued for public premises, as defined in Section 23039, who permits a person under the age of 21 years to enter and remain in the licensed premises without lawful business therein is guilty of a misdemeanor.
Any person under the age of 21 years who enters and remains in the licensed public premises without lawful business therein is guilty of a misdemeanor.

pc.pc: (a) Except as otherwise provided in subdivision (c), every person who sells, furnishes, gives, or causes to be sold, furnished, or given away any alcoholic beverage to any person under 21 years of age is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(c) Any person who violates subdivision (a) by purchasing any alcoholic beverage for, or furnishing, giving, or giving away any alcoholic beverage to, a person under 21 years of age, and the person under 21 years of age thereafter consumes the alcohol and thereby proximately causes great bodily injury or death to themselves or any other person, is guilty of a misdemeanor.

(d) Any on-sale licensee who knowingly permits a person under 21 years of age to consume any alcoholic beverage in the on-sale premises, whether or not the licensee has knowledge that the person is under 21 years of age, is guilty of a misdemeanor.

Anyone who sells, serves, consumes alcohol, or allows alcohol consumption at a licensed establishment during those hours, will be charged with a misdemeanor.

pc.pc: (a) A licensee shall not, at its licensed premises, sell, offer, or provide cannabis or cannabis products, as defined in Section 26001, including an alcoholic beverage that contains cannabis or a cannabis product, and no alcoholic beverage shall be manufactured, sold, or offered for sale if it contains tetrahydrocannabinol or cannabinoids, regardless of source.
(b) The department shall take disciplinary action against a licensee that violates this section, including, but not limited to, suspension or revocation of the license.

pc.pc: 25631: Any on- or off-sale licensee, or agent or employee of that licensee, who sells, gives, or delivers to any persons any alcoholic beverage or any person who knowingly purchases any alcoholic beverage between the hours of 2 o’clock a.m. and 6 o’clock a.m. of the same day, is guilty of a misdemeanor. For the purposes of this section, on the day that a time change occurs from Pacific standard time to Pacific daylight-saving time, or back again to Pacific standard time, “2 o’clock a.m.” means two hours after midnight of the day preceding the day such change occurs.

25362: Any retail licensee, or agent or employee of such licensee, who permits any alcoholic beverage to be consumed by any person on the licensee’s licensed premises during any hours in which it is unlawful to sell, give, or deliver any alcoholic beverage for consumption on the premises is guilty of a misdemeanor.

pc.pc: (a) It is unlawful for a person who is under the influence of any alcoholic beverage to drive a vehicle.
(b) It is unlawful for a person who has 0.08 percent or more, by weight, of alcohol in his or her blood to drive a vehicle.

For purposes of this article and Section 34501.16, percent, by weight, of alcohol in a person’s blood is based upon grams of alcohol per 100 milliliters of blood or grams of alcohol per 210 liters of breath.

In any prosecution under this subdivision, it is a rebuttable presumption that the person had 0.08 percent or more, by weight, of alcohol in his or her blood at the time of driving the vehicle if the person had 0.08 percent or more, by weight, of alcohol in his or her blood at the time of the performance of a chemical test within three hours after the driving.
(g) It is unlawful for a person who is under the combined influence of any alcoholic beverage and drug to drive a vehicle.

pc.pc: Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 24200, the department shall revoke a license upon any of the following grounds:

(a) If a retail licensee has knowingly permitted the illegal sale, or negotiations for the sales, of controlled substances or dangerous drugs upon his or her licensed premises. Successive sales, or negotiations for sales, over any continuous period of time shall be deemed evidence of permission.

As used in this section, “controlled substances” shall have the same meaning as is given that term in Article 1 (commencing with Section 11000) of Chapter 1 of Division 10 of the Health and Safety Code, and “dangerous drugs” shall have the same meaning as is given that term in Article 2 (commencing with Section 4015) of Chapter 9 of Division 2 of this code.

pc.pc: Although cannabis was legalized in California in 2018, there are still restrictions around its use, sale, and consumption. It is against the law to:
Smoke or ingest cannabis or cannabis products in public places or places where smoking tobacco is prohibited.
Smoke cannabis near schools, day care centers, or youth centers.

pc.pc: (b) For purposes of this section, the following definitions apply:

(2) “Smoke” means to inhale, exhale, burn, or carry any lighted or heated device or pipe, or any other lighted or heated cannabis or cannabis product intended for inhalation, whether natural or synthetic, in any manner or in any form. “Smoke” includes the use of an electronic smoking device that creates an aerosol or vapor, in any manner or in any form, or the use of any oral smoking device for the purpose of circumventing the prohibition of smoking in a place.
(4) “Youth center” has the same meaning as in Section 11353.1
(c) Nothing in this section shall be construed or interpreted to amend, repeal, affect, restrict, or preempt laws pertaining to the Compassionate Use Act of 1996.

pc.pc: (a) Section 11362.1 does not permit any person to:
(1) Smoke or ingest cannabis or cannabis products in a public place, except in accordance with Section 26200 of the Business and Professions Code.
(2) Smoke cannabis or cannabis products in a location where smoking tobacco is prohibited.

(3) Smoke cannabis or cannabis products within 1,000 feet of a school, day care center, or youth center while children are present at the school, day care center, or youth center, except in or upon the grounds of a private residence or in accordance with Section 26200 of the Business and Professions Code and only if such smoking is not detectable by others on the grounds of the school, day care center, or youth center while children are present.

pc.pc: Any product that is manufactured by
application of cannabinoid concentrate or extract to
commercially available candy or snack food items
without further processing of the product.
Commercially available
candy or snack food items may be used
as ingredients in a cannabis product,
provided that they are
used in a way that renders them
unrecognizable as the commercially available items
and the label, including the ingredient list, does not note that the final cannabis product contains the commercially available item;

of any kind;

pc.pc: The following types of products shall not be sold as cannabis products:
Alcoholic beverages
, as defined in section 23004 of the Business and Professions Code. This prohibition does not apply to tinctures that meet the requirements of Section 40308;
(b) Any
product containing any non-cannabinoid additive that would increase potency, toxicity, or addictive potential

, or that would create an unsafe combination with other psychoactive substances. Prohibited additives include, but are not limited to, nicotine and caffeine. This prohibition shall not apply to products containing naturally occurring caffeine, such as coffee, tea, or chocolate;

pc.pc: (c) Any cannabis
product that must be held at or below 41 degrees

Fahrenheit to keep it safe for human consumption, including, but not limited to, cream or custard-filled pies; pies or pastries which consist in whole or in part of milk or milk products, or eggs; and meat-filled pies or pastries. This prohibition shall not apply to juices or beverages that need to be held below 41 degrees Fahrenheit if the juice or beverage was processed in accordance with Section 40270, or to infused butter manufactured as permitted by subsection (g);
(d) Any
thermally processed low-acid cannabis product
packed in a hermetically sealed container that, if it were a food, would be subject to the manufacturing requirements of Title 21, Code of Federal Regulations, Part 113
(e) Any
acidified cannabis product
that, if it were a food, would be subject to the manufacturing requirements of Title 21, Code of Federal Regulations, Part 114;

pc.pc: Under its licensing role, the Department is responsible for issuing, suspending, and revoking alcoholic beverage licenses.
A license confers the licensee the privilege to sell alcohol and can also be suspended or revoked by the Department through administrative action if the establishment is found to be in violation.

ABC issues different types of liquor licenses depending on the type of establishment, the type of alcohol served, where it is consumed (on premises vs off premises), among other factors. ABC may also place reasonable conditions when issuing a license, such as hours of sale, display of signs, restrictions on entertainment, etc.

pc.pc: The TRACE protocol requires first responders to immediately notify the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) when an alcohol related emergency takes place if:
1. It involves a person under 21 where alcohol consumption caused great bodily injury or death OR
2. If anyone who was under the influence of alcohol is charged with vehicular manslaughter
Once ABC agents are alerted, an investigation begins to determine where the alcoholic beverage was purchased, acquired, or served.

Evidence is collected in the form of receipts, objects found in the vehicle, false IDs, bags, and statements from family members, friends, or employees of the establishment where the alcohol was obtained.
When the TRACE unit is quickly notified, the odds of a successful investigation are greater.

pc.pc: Per the California Penal Code, ABC agents are sworn peace officers in California.
All peace officers are agents with powers of arrest and authorized to enforce any penal provision of the law anywhere in the State of California.
They generally work in plain clothes and are in charge of investigating criminal and administrative violations of alcoholic beverage laws.

pc.pc: 830. Any person who comes within the provisions of this chapter and
who otherwise meets all standards imposed by law on a peace officer
is a peace officer, and notwithstanding any other provision of law,
no person other than those designated in this chapter is a peace
officer.
Persons employed by the Department of Alcoholic Beverage
Control
for the enforcement of Division 9 (commencing with Section
23000) of the Business and Professions Code and designated by the
Director of Alcoholic Beverage Control, provided that the primary
duty of any of these peace officers shall be the enforcement of the
laws relating to alcoholic beverages, as that duty is set forth in
Section 25755 of the Business and Professions Code.

pc.pc: Peace officers whether in uniform or plain clothes, have the right to visit and inspect any licensed establishments at any time during business hours.
The right to inspect is not dependent on probable cause or obtaining a warrant.
They can inspect extends to the bar, back bar, store room, office, closed or locked cabinets, safes, kitchen, or any other area within the licensed premises.
ABC agents may also inspect licensee records required to be kept under Business and Professions Code Division 9.
Interfering in any way with a peace officer’s right to inspect can result in arrest and license revocation.
Keep in mind that local jurisdictions (cities, counties) may have additional laws, ordinances or provisions that apply to an ABC licensed location in their area in addition to the statewide laws.

pc.pc: As you can probably guess, it is a lot easier to stop something before it happens than it is to fix it once things have gone awry.
Once a person becomes intoxicated, time is the only thing that can help them sober up.
On the bright side, there are many effective strategies you can use to keep them from becoming intoxicated in the first place.

pc.pc: As we mentioned earlier, alcohol absorption varies from one individual to another, depending on factors like amount of alcohol consumed, rate of consumption, food intake, gender, body composition, among others.
However, keep in mind that once alcohol is absorbed into the bloodstream the rate at which alcohol is broken down will be very similar across individuals.
Regardless of individual characteristics, such as weight or gender, alcohol is always metabolized at a rate of .
016 BAC
per hour

pc.pc: Not all alcoholic drinks are created equal, so how do we measure the strength of a drink? You have probably heard someone refer to a drink as 80 proof, or 100 proof, haven’t you?
Proof is a unit of measure used to indicate the amount of ethanol contained in a beverage.
To calculate the alcohol content or alcohol by volume (ABV) in any particular drink, all you have to do is divide the proof number by 2.
The result is the percentage of alcohol contained in that drink.
For example, a type of vodka said to be 80 proof, means that it contains 40% alcohol.

In other words, standard drinks help us keep track of how much alcohol we have served by ensuring we always serve the same amount of alcohol, regardless of the type of beverage ordered by a customer.

pc.pc: Don’t forget to consider the size and mixed drinks such as cocktails! Those can contain multiple servings of different types of alcohol.

Establishments can serve drinks that contain more than a single standard drink. In these cases, it is essential that you know the equivalencies, so that you are able to accurately calculate the number of drinks served to a customer.
Often, a glass of wine will contain more than the standard 5 ounces.
In order to calculate the number of standard drinks contained in an alcoholic beverage, just divide the number of ounces in the drink by the number of ounces contained in a standard drink.
Keep in mind that certain cocktails are made using more than just one type of liquor.
A Long Island iced tea, for example, is made by mixing vodka, rum, gin, tequila and triple sec!
That is well over one standard drink!

pc.pc: Since servers rely on standard drinks as a way of estimating alcohol intake, licensees must ensure that measuring devices are used in the establishment to ensure standard drink sizes for alcoholic beverages.
The size of an alcoholic drink equivalent is dependent upon the alcoholic beverage’s alcohol by volume or ABV.

Not only does this ensure the profitability of the establishment. It allows servers to keep track of how much alcohol has been served to a customer, and enforce and comply with policies against serving obviously intoxicated patrons.

pc.pc: Counting drinks is an extremely useful resource when estimating a person’s BAC and their level of intoxication.
However, we can’t deny that there will be times when you won’t be able to rely on counting drinks to determine how many drinks that person has had.

Your guests may come in having already had a few drinks elsewhere, another server may have served them at the bar earlier without you noticing, or they may be taking medication and are unaware of its interactions with alcohol.
Whatever the case, you must always stay sharp and use your observation and listening skills to gauge someone’s level of intoxication before you serve them alcohol.
This will prevent you from serving obviously intoxicated patrons.
To account for this, always be alert and observe their behavior and movements.
If you have reason to suspect that they are already intoxicated, politely explain that you will not be able to serve them any more alcohol.

pc.pc: Visibly intoxicated
is defined as a level of impairment that any person can detect by noticing the various visible signs of intoxication
Alcohol intoxication produces both behavioral and physical changes.
If your customer shows only one or two of these signs, that doesn’t necessarily mean they are intoxicated.
However, if they show a combination of them, it is very likely that they are drunk.

This will allow you to gather more information about their state, their plans for that night, and any intentions they may have of becoming intoxicated.
Now, let’s discuss the strategies you can implement to prevent a patron from becoming intoxicated.

Eating food can slow down the rate alcohol is absorbed into the bloodstream, so it’s always a good idea to encourage your guests to order a meal with their drinks.
Make an effort to actively promote this option. Your tip can only get bigger, after all.

pc.pc: Another strategy is to offer water. Salty foods and alcohol consumption can make the person dehydrated.
Remember, dehydration is one of the main factors that can contribute to a higher BAC.
In addition to this, a thirsty customer may start ordering more drinks to quench his thirst and become intoxicated.
Always serve water with every drink.

pc.pc: Don’t overserve.
Discourage binge drinking by serving only one drink at a time. In doing so, you are slowing down the consumption rate.
Also, your company or establishment might have a policy in regards to over-serving.
Check with your manager or supervisor if you are not sure.

pc.pc: Don’t overpour. If you are a bartender, do not pour more alcohol than the recipe calls for.
If you serve a stronger drink, the guest might not be able to regulate his drinking and become intoxicated.
In doing so, you also make it difficult for a server to keep track of how many drinks the customer has actually had.

pc.pc: Offer Attractively Priced Non-alcoholic beverages. Some establishments offer non-alcoholic drinks at a slightly lower price.
You can suggest it as an appealing substitute when you notice that someone already has already had a few drinks.

This is also a good option for designated drivers looking to partake in the social aspect of drinking while limiting their alcohol consumption. You can also offer special promotions for the designated driver in the group.

pc.pc: Don’t Encourage Binge Drinking.
Never offer happy hour specials that may encourage unhealthy drinking patterns or unlawful discrimination, such as bottomless alcoholic drinking specials or ladies night.
If the establishment offers a happy hour menu, make sure to include attractive food choices or food specials as well.

pc.pc: How about happy hour? Happy hour refers to the common business practice of offering alcoholic beverages and or food at a reduced price during certain hours of the day.
Although this practice is illegal in some states, establishments in California are allowed to sell food and drink combinations for a promotional discounted price.
The only restriction is that the drink must not be complimentary, so it is against the law to offer free drinks or two-for-one specials.
Now that we have learned about various best practices, let’s put your knowledge to the test with a specific scenario.

pc.pc: Bartender: Hey guys! What can I get you?
Eric: I’d like the pale ale beer and your shredded beef tacos.
Bartender: Great choice! Those are my favorite. How about you sir?
Jeff : Mmmm… no food for me. Just a double whiskey on the rocks.
Bartender: Coming right up.
Eric: Our team better crush it tonight, or I’ll start re-thinking my loyalty to those guys.
Jeff: Yeah. No joke.
Bartender: Here you go guys. Let me know if I can get you anything else.
Eric: Thanks, man.
Bartender: You got it.
Eric: Oh come on! How did he miss that pass?
Jeff: This game sucks. I need another drink.
Bartender: Not a great night for the team, eh?
Jeff: You’re telling me.
Bartender: So, how can I help you?
Jeff: Can I get another double whiskey on the rocks? And one for my friend. I have a feeling we’re going to need it.

pc.pc: Hard to tell, isn’t it? Looks can be deceiving.

As you should already know, 21 is the minimum age for a person to legally purchase or consume alcohol in California. Serving alcohol to a minor is a serious criminal offense that can have severe implications for a business and its employees.
Regardless of how old they look, always check a patron’s ID before serving them.

If a server inspects someone’s ID and concludes that it is legally acceptable, and the minor looks like he could be twenty one or older, the alcohol server has a defense to any charges for selling alcohol to a minor even if the ID turns out to be fake.
Don’t jeopardize your job or the establishment’s liquor license!

pc.pc: Here are the three golden rules to follow:
Always ask patrons for their ID. It doesn’t matter how old they look or how busy you are. You should never skip this step.
Make sure that the ID shown is both a valid and acceptable form of ID.
Verify the ID belongs to the guest.
Since some people look older than their age, many establishments adhere to a strict policy of 'We card anyone under 35'.
Check with your manager to see if your establishment follows this rule.

pc.pc: Now, you may be wondering what qualifies as an acceptable ID.

As a general rule, you will be looking for documents issued by a federal or State government agency, all of which include the name, date of birth, a photograph, a physical description of the person in question, and a valid expiration date.
Only the following documents are considered an acceptable form of ID.
State issued driver’s licenses (from California or another State)
State-issued Identification Card
Driver’s license from another state
Government issued Passports (even if they don’t include a physical description of the ID holder)
Military ID (even if it doesn’t include a physical description of the ID holder)
Expired IDs, obviously altered IDs, temporary driver licenses, IDs that belong to someone else, or IDs issued by schools or employers are not a valid form of ID.

pc.pc: Step 2 - Ask for the ID
When inspecting an ID, always make sure you’re holding it in your hand.
You will not be able to conduct a proper examination unless you are able to take a closer look.
If a patron shows you an ID that is visible from their wallet, politely ask them to take it out and hand it to you.
Then, proceed to examine the front and back of the ID.

pc.pc: Step 1 - Observe the customer’s behavior.
Do they show any signs of nervousness or intoxication?

Since they may be afraid of getting caught, minors trying to get into a bar or order drinks using a fake ID will often come across as fidgety or restless, so be on the lookout for that type of behavior.

pc.pc: Step 4 - Check the Expiration Date
All driver licenses include an expiration date, which usually matches the person’s birth date.
Since minors will frequently attempt to use a relative’s expired ID, it is important that you always verify that the ID has not expired.
Remember, expired licenses should never be accepted as valid. Even if it's only been a few days

pc.pc: Step 3 - Check for any signs of tampering
Does the ID look like it’s been damaged?
Any anomalies in the lamination, such as bubbles, creases, or tears, are often signs of an ID which has either been altered or is counterfeit.
If the ID feels thinner or thicker than usual, this could mean it has been re-laminated.
The edges should feel smooth to the touch. You should not be able to peel it apart.
A photograph that appears raised or altered, alterations to the birth date, or a signature written in ink, are also indicators that the ID is fake or has been tampered with.

pc.pc: Step 5. Inspect the security features. When inspecting an ID, do so in good lighting.
Although it’s true that some forgeries are almost indistinguishable from genuine IDs, there are some security features you can use to determine whether an ID is real.
Some of these features visible by UV light or flashlight include holograms, UV images or text, tactile features, laser perforation, magnetic strips, and microprint.
We will explain each of these features in more detail.

pc.pc: Step 6 - Does the ID belong to the Guest?
Now that you have verified that the ID is not a counterfeit, you must also make sure it belongs to the guest. Here are a few things to check for.
Photograph

- Take a moment to carefully notice if the person portrayed in the ID looks like the guest in front of you. Pay attention to things that cannot be easily changed, such as their hairline, nose, chin, or ears and check if they match.
Physical Description
- Check that the person’s appearance matches the features described on the ID. Although hair color and facial hair may change frequently, features such as eye color or height usually do not change.
Date of Birth

- Look at the date of birth and ask yourself if the appearance of the guest is consistent with that age. If based on the date of birth, this person should be 45 years old, but the guest clearly looks like they are barely 21, you are most likely looking at a tampered or fake ID.

pc.pc: The Federal REAL ID Act created new requirements around the forms of ID that could be used to board flights and enter secure federal facilities.
A California Real ID driver’s license or identification card can be obtained from the DMV and requires applicants to show proof of identity and proof of California residency.
A California REAL ID can be recognized by a gold bear and star in the top right corner of the ID.
Other features include:
The state seal
A magnetic strip on the back of the ID
The birthdate embossed on the holder's picture
Vertical format to indicate the holder is under 21 years of age, along with the words "Age 21 in" a specific year.

pc.pc: A valid California Federal Non-Compliant ID can also be obtained at the DMV. The difference is that it may not be used to board flights after May 2023 or enter secure federal facilities.
You can identify a California Federal Non-Compliant ID by looking at the top right corner of the ID. Instead of the gold bear and the star, you will find the phrase: “Federal Limits Apply”
There is also a barcode located on the back of a valid California driver license.

pc.pc: Now that you know what to look for in a valid and acceptable form of ID, let's look at an easy way to calculate someone’s age based on their date of birth.
Look at the birth year shown on the ID and add 20.
In this example, it’s 1989, so let’s try:
Then, add 1
That is the year when the person will have turned 21.

pc.pc: If this seems too complicated, you can just take the current year, subtract 21 and remember that year.
For example, if the current year is 2023, all you have to do is remember 2002.

If the birth year is 2002, but the birth date is later than today’s date, he or she is also still a minor.

pc.pc: Michael: Hey! Good evening, ladies. How can I help you?
Donna: Ummm…can… can I please get an apple martini?
Amy: And I’ll have whatever your favorite cocktail is. Your reputation precedes you. So, surprise me!
Michael: Haha. Well, I’m very flattered. Can I just see some ID please?
Amy: Ummm… okay… sure.
Donna: Are you serious? We come here all the time.
Michael: I’m sorry, but it’s our policy. I could lose my job if I don’t ask for your ID and you turn out to be under 21.
Donna: Great…well, I left mine at home. Thanks for ruining my night.
Amy: It’s ok. Here’s mine. But I gotta be honest. If you weren’t so good looking, I’d be annoyed too.
Michael: [talking to himself]: Hmmm out of state. I’m not sure what a valid driver license is supposed to look like in Oklahoma, but these girls look pretty young to me.

pc.pc: If you are not sure about the validity of an ID, ask the guest about the personal information shown on their ID, such as their address, their height, or astrological sign.
If they get nervous and are not able to answer these questions, there is a pretty good chance that the ID is not valid or belongs to someone else.

pc.pc: Another option is to ask the guest for an alternate form of ID, such as a credit card, and ask them for a fresh signature to compare to the one on the ID.
However, if after asking a couple of questions, you are still not sure about the validity of the ID being presented, it is best to err on the side of prevention and refuse service.
Per Section 25659 of the California Business and Professions Code, servers have the right to refuse alcohol service to any individual if he or she cannot produce proof of being 21 years or older.
Now, let’s go back to Michael and the two college girls.

pc.pc: Michael: So, Amy. What’s your address?
Amy: Uh…135 Pine Street… Ooops, no. Wait. Pine Avenue. Is that it? I just moved… like… last month. I already forgot my old address.
Michael: Ah! Really? And what is your astrological sign?
Amy: Uh… That’s random….but….uh…. I’m a Leo
Michael: Well, according to the date of birth on your driver’s license, you should be a Pisces.
Amy: Oh wow! You know? I’m terrible at remembering those things.
Michael: Yup. These girls are definitely underage, and the ID Amy is showing me is most likely fake.

The minor may attempt to order alcohol from a different staff member.
By alerting your manager you are preventing them from succeeding.

pc.pc: It is always a good idea to document these types of incidents.

If the girl is served alcohol at a different bar later that night, having proof that service was refused at your establishment can protect you and your establishment from any potential liability if the authorities get involved.
The minor may attempt to order alcohol from a different staff member.
By alerting your manager and other servers, you are preventing the minor from succeeding in this attempt.
As you will learn in this training, communicating with other team members can make a huge difference when dealing with problematic situations.

pc.pc: California law does not require that you confiscate counterfeit IDs, so you will not be liable in any way if you choose not to.
It is up to every establishment to decide on their own policy for dealing with counterfeit IDs.
If you aren’t sure, talk to your manager to learn more about the rules and policies at your establishment.
If you do confiscate an ID, you are required by law to provide the guest with a receipt and to turn the fake ID over to the local authority within 24 hours of being confiscated.
Now let’s watch another potential scenario you may encounter.

pc.pc: Sean: Good evening. My name is Sean and I'll be your server tonight. Can I get you started with something to drink?
David: I’ll have a glass of your house Chardonnay.
Sheila: And I’d like to try the raspberry margarita.
Sean: Would you mind if I take a quick look at both your IDs?
David: Not a problem. Here you go. I’m 23 and she’s 20. But don’t worry-she’s my wife, so I take full responsibility for her.

pc.pc: Before we wrap things up, it's important to mention that ID readers are one of the most commonly used tools to check if an ID is valid. The most popular ones work by scanning the magnetic band on the ID, and showing the person’s information on the display screen.
However, be aware that some fake IDs will even have the magnetic band with information encoded on it and may, at first glance, pass the test.

While some of the more sophisticated ID checkers are able to scan for many of the security features mentioned earlier, remember that you must still physically check that the information displayed by the reader matches the details on the front of the ID and the characteristics of the person in front of you.

pc.pc: Before we dive in, it is important to reiterate the importance of teamwork and communication.
An establishment will be far more effective when the entire staff works together to identify intoxicated patrons and defuse potentially risky situations.
This includes servers, bartenders, managers, valets, hosts and hostesses, security staff, and anyone else who interacts with the customer.
Always talk to your team if you notice a guest who is visibly intoxicated or has arrived to the establishment already intoxicated.

pc.pc: Remember to always follow company policy and standard procedures when handling these situations.
If you are not sure what these are, ask your manager.
However, there are some clear-cut scenarios where you must always refuse service
· If a patron shows an invalid ID
· If a patron becomes belligerent
· If someone requests to be served alcohol outside the hours of operation
· If a patron is a habitual drunkard
If a patron is obviously intoxicated with alcohol or any other substance, such as medication, or recreational or illegal drugs.
Or whenever you are unsure about any of these factors.

pc.pc: Richard
Hi.
Joe: Hey! How’s it going? What can I get for you?
Richard: Could I please get a bourbon on the rocks?
Joe: Absolutely. Anything else?
Richard: No. Thanks. Just that, for now.
Joe: Excellent. Could I please see your ID?
Richard: Yes. Of course. Here it is.
Joe: Thank you very much. Please feel free to grab a table and I’ll bring your drink there.
Richard: Great. Thanks. I’m not waiting for anyone, so I’ll just grab a seat here, if you don’t mind.
Joe: I think that’s a great idea.
Joe: Here you go. Let me know if I can get you anything else.
Richard: Thanks.
Joe: How are you doing sir? Can I get you anything else?
Richard: Same as before. Just make it a double this time, please.
Joe: No problem. Would you like an appetizer with that? Our hot dogs are really good.
Richard. I appreciate the suggestion, but I’m not that hungry. Thanks.
Richard
[slurring words]:
Good evening, beautiful ladies! Mind if I join you?
Trisha: Uh… actually yes. Sorry. We’re kind of happy on our own tonight.
Richard: Ah! I see. You think you’re too good to talk to me? Fine. It’s not like I’m trying to hit on you or anything.
Trisha What a jerk!
Joe: Hey! Still doing okay?
Richard:
[slurring words and speaking loudly]
Yeah. I’m enjoying this blue martini. The other bartender recommended it. I think you guys are my new best friends.
Richard: Come on, love birds! Loosen up!
Jason: Back off, weirdo!
Richard: Hey there, old friends! I’ve got moves. Check it out. I bet you wanna talk to me now, don’t you? eh?
Richard: Hey buddy! Can you fix me another one of those…err… what’s it called….oh yeaaaaah… the blue martini. Sooo good….

pc.pc: Joe: Give me just a minute please.
Joe: Hey Rob
Rob: Hey! What’s going on?

Joe: I don’t know if you saw him out there, but the guy with the beard had a bit too much to drink. He keeps walking up to people and trying to dance with them, and some of the customers seem pretty annoyed already. I think maybe it’s time to kick him out.
Rob: Oh I see. Hmm let me handle this. Just show me where he is.
Joe: Sure. Thanks.
Rob: Hey there!
Richard: Hey! So where’s my drink?
Rob: I’m sorry sir, but by law, we are not allowed to serve you any more alcohol.
Richard: What?! That is the dumbest thing I’ve ever heard. I’m paying for it!
Rob: No. It’s not that. We care about you, and just want to make sure you get home safely tonight.
Richard: Well… you’re not my mother, are you?
Rob: Of course not, but I bet you can’t say no to a bowl of nachos on the house. And if I may make a suggestion, the virgin mojito is very refreshing and one of our best. Would you like to try that?
Richard: Errr… ok. That’s nice of you, I guess. I am kinda hungry now.
Rob: Excellent.

pc.pc: Joe: I’m sorry. I won’t be able to serve you anything else.
Richard: What do you mean? Why?
Joe: Well, you’re really drunk and also disturbing other customers.
Richard: No, you’re lying! I’m your customer and I’m paying to have a good time here!
Joe: I apologize, but I’m going to have to ask you to leave.
Richard: This is unacceptable! Sure. I’ll leave. But I’m never coming back to this hellhole.

pc.pc: Remember to Alert Other Team Members.
When you notice signs of intoxication in a guest, communicate the situation to other servers. Identify the patron, and the reasons why you decided to stop service.

This is important because, once you inform the customer that you will no longer serve them alcohol, he or she may attempt to order alcohol from another server. If they know that the patron has been “cut off,” they won’t make the mistake of serving them.
In addition to this, other team members can provide backup by stepping in if needed. They can help by calling the customer a cab, etc.

pc.pc: Convey empathy and use non-confrontational language
Never tell the customer that he or she is drunk, as this will embarrass and upset them.
Avoid passing judgement on their behavior, while trying to be friendly, non-judgmental, and courteous instead.
When communicating your decision to stop service, try to relate to their frustration and focus on expressing your concern for their safety.
Use ‘I’ statements to convey that you value and care about the guest, such as: 'As our guest, I would like to make sure that you make it home safely tonight'.

Focus on your duty and liability as a server, by making statements such as: 'It is illegal for me to serve you more alcohol', ‘Our policy doesn’t allow me to serve any more alcohol', or 'If I pour another drink, I could lose my job’.

pc.pc: Always be firm and assertive. Once you decide to cut someone off, you must stand by your decision and not bargain with the guest who may try to convince you to serve “just one more drink”.

pc.pc: Offer Food or Non-Alcoholic Beverages.
When you inform the guest that you will no longer be serving alcohol, they may feel unwelcome, embarrassed, and excluded from their group of friends.
By offering a substitute, you are showing hospitality and helping them continue to partake in the fun.

pc.pc: Whenever possible, it is also a good idea to try to get their friends on your side.
If your guest is accompanied by others, try to speak to them privately when the intoxicated guest leaves the table. The most sober friend is usually your best bet.
Since they’re people that the guest likes and trusts, they may be able to effectively dissuade the guest from ordering another drink.
This may save you the awkwardness of informing the guest that you will have to stop service, or at least ease some of the tension if you do have to bring it up.

pc.pc: Take precautions to ensure their safety when leaving the premises.
Before you allow an intoxicated guest to leave the establishment, make sure that he or she is not driving.
Then, see to it that the guest has access to a safe means of transportation to go home, such as a ride from a friend or a cab.
Let's take a look at a true story that illustrates the importance of following this last step.

pc.pc: INTOXICATED PATRON DROWNS AFTER BEING KICKED OUT OF LOCAL BAR
A 24-year old man was kicked out of a local bar due to alcohol intoxication.
At the time of the incident, the bar staff did not allow him to retrieve his coat or let his friends know he was leaving.

pc.pc: It looks like her mind is made up, so he should avoid arguing with her. Since she has confirmed that she won’t be driving, she is not a danger to anyone. Jessica: Sorry, Lindsay. After the drinks we had back at Josh’s place, I’m afraid I can’t possibly keep up with you.
Lindsay: Blah blah blah…. You don’t know how to have fun. I’ll drink it. Can’t let it go to waste.
Josh: Ok, wild girl, but you may want to slow down after this one.
Lindsay suffered from alcohol poisoning. She had been drinking at her friend’s house and at the restaurant.
When the paramedics showed up, her BAC was 0.20
She was hospitalized. But luckily, she recovered. The server had to pay a fine and serve 30 days in jail.

pc.pc: Matt: I am truly sorry, but even if you won’t be driving, I’m still concerned for your well-being.
Lindsay: But I have a driver! Right, Josh??
Josh: Yeah, man. I already told you.

Ashley: He is right. It's against our company policy, and against the law to serve you more alcohol. Our restaurant could be held liable. But most importantly, we take the safety of our guests very seriously.
You could still take advantage of our happy hour menu and get the chicken wings. They are to die for.
Josh: That’s fine. We understand.

It doesn’t matter how many drinks you serve to a customer or if they confirmed that they won’t be driving. Once you notice signs of intoxication, it is illegal to continue to serve alcohol.

pc.pc: You may be wondering about the designated driver mentioned in the previous scenario. A designated driver is a person who agrees not to consume any alcoholic beverages in order to drive the other members of the group home safely.
However, even if there is a designated driver in the group, it is still illegal for you to serve alcohol to other members of the group if you suspect that they are intoxicated.
A designated driver should not be an excuse for anyone to drink until they pass out. Remember, it is both illegal and dangerous to serve alcohol to obviously intoxicated customers.

pc.pc: Bartender: Hey Laura. I think it’s time to stop service to the guy over there.
Laura: Yes. Definitely. I don’t know why we let him get so intoxicated in the first place.
Bartender: Well, he said he was waiting for someone and ordered a bottle of wine. Turns out, that other someone never showed up.
Laura: I see. Ok. Keep an eye on him. And let me know if you need me to step in.
Cole: Hey!
Bartender: What can I do for you sir?
Cole:
[slurring words]
Finally! I’ve been trying to get someone’s attention for a while. Another bottle of the same wine. This one's empty.
Bartender: How about I bring you some food instead? Would you like to take a look at the menu?
Guy: No... no... just the red wine.
Bartender: I apologize, but I won’t be able to serve you more alcohol tonight.
Guy: Wha... what are you talking about?
Bartender: If I serve you another drink, I could lose my job sir. I hope you understand. We are just looking out for your safety.
Guy: What kind of idiotic blabber are you spitting out? Can’t you see I’m a grown man? Spare me the...sermon and get me what I’m willing to pay for... I’m not in the mood for this kind of crap.
Bartender: I’m truly sorry. Let me get my manager so she can talk to you.
Guy: I see. This is personal, isn’t it? Let’s take this outside! I’ll show you why it’s a bad idea to disrespect me like that!

pc.pc: You should also avoid confrontation. If the customer becomes violent or threatening, and you believe he is becoming a danger to you or other guests, walk away and don’t hesitate to call the police.
They have more experience than you and are qualified to handle these situations adequately. Keep in mind you might need to complete an incident report if it is a company requirement.

It is very important not to underestimate the potential danger when you witness signs of violent behavior. These situations usually escalate very quickly, and can lead to very serious and fatal consequences.
Let's take a look at a real-life case that illustrates this.

pc.pc: When it comes to intoxicated patrons, alcohol is not the only possible cause.
Patrons may become intoxicated as a result of using other substances, such as medications, recreational, or illegal drugs.
These drugs fall into 3 main categories based on the effect they have: depressants, stimulants, and hallucinogenic drugs, also known as psychedelics

pc.pc: Depressants have an effect on the central nervous system, slowing down its functions and the communication between the brain and the body.

This results in slower heart rate, slower respiratory system, slower digestion, among other changes. Doctors may prescribe these substances to help manage certain conditions, such as anxiety, insomnia, or seizures. However, many people use them for recreational purposes.

<Style FontFamily="Articulate Light" FontSize="28" ForegroundColor="lt1,00" LinkColor="lt1,00" />

· Nicotine (tobacco)
· Caffeine

pc.pc: Signs that someone is under the influence of a stimulant drug include:
· Restlessness
· Tremors
· Dilated pupils
· Sweating
· Euphoria
· Reduced inhibition
· Fidgeting
· Hypersensitivity to sight, sound, and touch
· And, in some cases, paranoia

pc.pc: Hallucinogens, also called psychedelics, alter the way we perceive reality.
They have an effect on the five senses, altering the way things look, smell, taste, hear, or feel.

pc.pc: Signs that someone is under the influence of a hallucinogen include:
· Hallucinations and distorted perception of shape and sizes of objects.
· Feelings of euphoria
· Drowsiness
· Difficulty concentrating
· Impaired communication skills
· Nausea and vomiting
· Lack of coordination
· Agitation or paranoia

If a violation occurs on the licensed premises, both the establishment and the licensee are at risk of administrative penalties, such as fines or suspension or revocation.

pc.pc: According to Title 4 California Code of Regulations 144, when the CA Department of ABC is

“reaching a decision on a disciplinary action under the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act (Bus. and Prof. Code Sections 23000,et seq.), and the Administrative Procedures Act (Govt. Code Sections 11400,et seq.), the Department is to consider the disciplinary guidelines entitled "Penalty Guidelines" (dated 12/17/2003). However, the Department may deviate] from these guidelines if it determines that a deviation is warranted based on the presence of aggravating or mitigating factors.”

This means that the Department will generally follow the penalties outlined in the penalty schedule for first time offenses. However, depending on the presence or absence of mitigating or aggravating factors unique to each establishment, the Department may impose higher or lower penalties.
